main_text.l: traxerat, non amplius quam octo comitantibus ad Ammonitas confugit. Igitur populum universum metus pervaserat, ne paucorum scelus omnium exitio rex Babylonius ultimum iret. nam praeter Godoliam, multos ex Chaldeis cum eo interfecerant. Iraq; consilium ineunt fugiendi in Aegyptum. Sed prius Ieremiam frequentes adeunt, sciscitantes divinum responsum. At ille verbis Dei universos hortari, in solo patrio manerent: si id fecissent, Dei praesidio tuendos nullumque a Babyloniis periculum fore. Sin Aegyptum petierent, omnes ibi ferro ac fame diversoque mortis genere perituros. Sed plebs assueto malo in-solens parēdi salubribus consiliis, & divi-no imperio, profecta est in Aegyptum. Quid de ea postea actū sacris litteris [illegible, ~8 letters]: nobis nihil compertum. Hoc tractu temporū Nabuchodonosor, elatus rebus secundis, statuam sibi auream immensae magnitudinis posuit, adorarique eam ut sacram effigie praecepit. Quod cum certatim ab omnibus depravatis adulatione omnium animis fieret, Ananias, Azarias & Misael prophano officio abstinuerunt, non ignorantes honorem hunc soli Deo debitum.

page.notes: The page number reads like "9f" in the scan, most likely 91; marked [?]. The word after "litteris" is not legible: it appears to be a short verb of about eight letters, possibly "silentur", but I could not read it, so I left it illegible. "omnium" after "adulatione" is partly rubbed; the spelling is uncertain. The marginal note "Iosephus Ant. l.10. c.11." sits beside the line "divi-no imperio" and is placed at the end of that sentence. The long s is rendered as plain s throughout, so "confilium" is given as "consilium", "afsueto" as "assueto", and "Mifael" as "Misael". The marginal note "Ierem. 44" sits beside the line "malo in-". The hyphens "in-" and "divi-" are printed line-end hyphens and are kept.
